description: Functions PASSED, CALLED, or handed to a host call do not fire E-VALUE-FUNCTION-STORED (§14.3). `twice` is passed to a scrml function and to `.map` as a callback, called to produce a map value, and appears in an object literal written DIRECTLY as a host-JS call argument (`console.log({ double: twice })` — the host boundary). The clean twin of e-value-function-stored-pos.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S462 "a" (functions still flow PASSED and CALLED) + S462 "go on the package" item 3 (host boundary)
rationale: §14.3 a function may be PASSED (argument, callback) or CALLED; a literal written directly as a host-JS call argument is at the boundary and not judged. None of these stores a function in a scrml value.
